utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Will the registrar call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This is case number IT-98-32/1-PT, the Prosecutor versus Milan Lukic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In light of the amendment of the indictment against Mr. Lukic, we are here to give him the opportunity to tender pleas to the amended charges, and what I propose to do is to invite him to plead in respect of all the charges against him for the avoidance of any doubt about the effect of the amendments. Before we proceed to that, there are one or two formalities to be dealt with. First of all, Mr. Lukic, can you confirm to me that you're hearing the proceedings in a language which you understand? We need the microphone, I think, so that you can answer properly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can -- can you now hear what I'm saying to you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I hear and I can understand what you're saying, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And can you hear it in a language which you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry about that technical difficulty. It sounds as though things are okay, but if you at any stage do not hear clearly in your own language what is being said by any of the parties here, please draw my attention to it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, can I ascertain who appears this morning. For the Prosecution first of all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Mark Harmon, Fergal Gaynor, and case manager Lise-Lotte Karlsson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harmon. Mr. Karnavas, would you identify yourself, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Michael Karnavas for Mr. Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, Mr. Lukic, what will now happen is that the court deputy will read to you just a very brief summary of each of the charges that you now face on the new indictment, and at the end of each little summary - it's only a few words in each case - he will ask, Do you plead guilty or not guilty? And you should indicate to him the nature of the plea, whether you plead guilty or not guilty. Now, do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And just one thing -- I probably jumped ahead of myself. Mr. Karnavas, I should have confirmed with you, as was indicated to me informally that the accused was happy to waive the right of the indictment read in full to him at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, for reminding us all. I was worried a little bit. Yes, I did want to indicate that we waive the reading of the indictment. He has been advised of his rights and I know that he will do so very shortly, but on his behalf I enter "not guilty" to all the charges. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: While that sounds like a very sensible way to proceed, the traditional practice here is at least to summarise each of the charges individually and to take a plea from the accused on each charge individually. Now, while this is done, Mr. Lukic, could you stand up, please. The court deputy will now read each charge individually and you should tender your plea one by one.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 1, persecutions, a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 2, murder, a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 3, murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 21, cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please be seated, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In view of the pleas that have been tendered, I invite the Registrar to arrange a trial in due course, although I understand there are other proceedings also ongoing in relation to this particular accused. The effect of the decision in relation to the amendment of the indictment is that Mr. Lukic has until the 21st of April to file any preliminary motions in terms of Rule 50(C), and the Prosecution will have 14 days after that to file any response. Beyond that, I do not think there are any procedural issues that I have to address. Mr. Harmon, is there anything else you wish to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't wish to raise anything, Your Honour, but I do understand that Mr. Lukic did have something that he wished to raise with the Trial Chamber -- or the Pre-Trial Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, Mr. Karnavas advises me there is something you wish to address me on. What is that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I'm not quite clear on the matter of the attorneys and an adequate defence, and for those purposes I would like to have Mr. Karnavas as my Defence counsel, but since the Registry did not grant my request, I would like to ask the Trial Chamber and the Registry that if Mr. Karnavas is not able to be the chief Defence counsel, for at least -- that he at least be in the team because he's familiar with my case, right from the beginning, since my address and my extradition from Argentina. So in order to have an adequate, proper defence, I would like to have Mr. Karnavas in the team if he's not able to be the lead counsel. This is what I wanted to address you on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Karnavas, do you want to comment on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very briefly, Your Honour. Mr. Lukic and I go back as early as November last year. I did assist him throughout the proceedings. I had met with -- I had contact the Prosecution on his behalf before he came here. Mr. Lukic was denied having access to me on his arrival, which caused some concern. Thereafter, there are some things that happened that caused him to lose confidence in the way the Registry is handling the situation. In any event, I've indicated to the Registry that, in my opinion, there is not a scheduling conflict and I'm able to assist in light of the procedure that is already put in motion in regards to this case, but they've sought -- they think otherwise. Mr. Lukic, in any event, has asked me if I would stay on, either as a co-counsel or as a consultant. I had indicated to him that I would -- you know, I have no objections to that, I would assist him. I am familiar with the case. We have begun a particular procedure that we think that can resolve this case in an expeditious manner to everyone's satisfaction. I think that's the most important thing. And now it's up to the Registry and His Honour to decide. He is concerned about the situation with respect to Argentina. I'm now told by the Registry that that is an open issue, that the Registry never made guarantees to the government of Argentina that he would not be transferred to Sarajevo. This is news to Mr. Lukic. I've sought disclosure material from the Registry. We have not received it. I'm told that perhaps I'm being overzealous in representing Mr. Lukic at this stage since I'm not his permanent counsel, although, as counsel of record, I think I'm obligated to carry out whatever instructions are given to me so long as they're ethical and within the Rules of Procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But if you were to fall into the category of consultant, as you describe it, is there a funding difficulty?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Pardon?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If you fall into the category of consultant, as you've described it, is there is not then a funding difficulty?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, the funding difficulty would be -- as I understand, we now have this lump-sum system and it would be within the lead counsel to -- you know, to remunerate. There's a funding problem, to start with, with every case here, but, you know, but it's not matter of funding and us asking for additional funds, it's a matter of Mr. Lukic wanting me on the team to assist on -- to guide him through the process. He has met with two very good lawyers, both of whom I recommended for him to choose, so I'm confident in his choice, whoever he chooses. I've worked with them, I've had long associations with them, and so I'm willing to work with either one and, of course, assist the Trial Chamber in any capacity that I can, but I leave it up to the Registry, and I leave it up to the Trial Chamber. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Well, I think I have a clear understanding of the issue involved. It's not something I can deal with at this stage, but I will consider whether there is anything I can do on the matter; and if there is, then you'll be alerted to what action I think I can take. Thank you, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will inform the Court that it is our position that Mr. Karnavas has a conflict of interest in representing this defendant and representing defendants -- a past defendant. We have made that clear in correspondence to Mr. Karnavas. There have been discussions about that. While we agree to disagree, our position is there is a conflict of interest, and our position is that Mr. Karnavas's continued association in the case will create difficulties for us in terms of resolving the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may briefly respond to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Hold on. First of all, Mr. Harmon, are you aware of the basis on which the Registry have taken the stance that they have taken?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I am not, Your Honour. I'm informing the Court of an independent and separate issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Because that's not the message I was getting from -- from the submissions made. I didn't form the impression it was an issue of conflict of interest in the sense of a previous case. I understood what was being submitted to me was a conflict of commitments rather than a conflict of interest. Now, have I understood that correctly, Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You have. If I may respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: With respect to the Registry, their issue is that there is a scheduling conflict. So that's that. With respect to the Prosecution, they have sent two letters. They say that there is a conflict of interest. They don't say what that conflict of interest is other than I represented Mr. Blagojevic in one case, and they believe that Mr. Lukic may have been involved in Srebrenica. They haven't provided any specific evidence. They haven't shown anything. I've met with them; they haven't said anything of the sort. I'm waiting for it. He hasn't been indicted. There is nothing in the indictment with respect to Srebrenica. So until such time -- and I'm -- by the way, I spent three years working nonstop on that case. In my professional opinion, there is no conflict of interest as of yet. Now if they have information which I don't have that reveals that, I'll be the first one to withdraw. I understand my ethical obligations. So I just want to make that very, very clear. Having said that, I also want to point out to Mr. Harmon, because he may not be aware of this, that currently there is a lead counsel in Srebrenica who was also involved in the Blagojevic case, representing, as lead counsel, Mr. Jokic. So there seems to be sort of a flexible approach in how they see these conflicts of interests. If they see an advocate perhaps that they don't want to have on the one side, they may say there is a conflict of interest. On the other hand, they may take a more flexible approach. I don't know. But I can tell you that if we're going to go down that route, then at least they should present specific evidence, let me look at it, and as a professional, I will withdraw. But as of the moment, I have not seen any evidence that gives me any discomfort that I have a conflict of interest. And as a long-time public defender, I'm fully aware of what a conflict of interest is. And I'm willing to sit down with Mr. Harmon. On a confidential basis, he can disclose to me what he believes the conflict to be. I think we're both reasonable individuals. I know I am, and I have no reason to believe that he's not. So -- you know, and I'm sure he is. So that's my position, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karnavas. Mr. Harmon, do you want to say any more about the nature of this conflict?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was involved also in the Srebrenica prosecutions and I'm familiar with the evidence, as is Mr. Karnavas. I don't care to say more about it at this point in time. Mr. Karnavas is familiar with the evidence. He's familiar with the intercepts. I'd be glad to provide that to Mr. Karnavas, and we will continue some discussions in this respect, but I will inform the Court that our view is -- it's a firm view, and our view is one that is that if Mr. Karnavas is involved in this case, a resolution of this case, because of the conflict of interest, will be problematic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, it's all a mystery to me. Obviously the previous involvement of a counsel in a related case or a case with crossover evidence, similar evidence, almost identical case, does not necessarily amount to a conflict of interest. So there must be something in there that, for good reason, no doubt, it's inappropriate for us to be discussing here. But one thing I can say, Mr. Harmon, from the sense I have of where this case maybe going, that this should be resolved one way or another quickly. This case, or the case relating to this accused has a knock-on effect on that of his co-accused. It inevitably has a knock-on effect on the overall business of the Tribunal, and at the moment we seem to have an accused and a willing counsel who wish to talk to you positively about how this matter might progress. Therefore, it seems to me in the interests of everyone to knock out of the way any barriers. And what Mr. Karnavas appears to be offering is the opportunity to discuss that, the barrier that you see in the way, and an opportunity to try and decide one way or the other whether it's insurmountable or not. So I hope that following today that discussion can take place rapidly. I think that I will, nevertheless, hoping that it will be resolved one way or the other, apply my mind to the issue of the Registry, and if there is something I think that I can raise or attend to there, then I will attend to it. Now, is there anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Nothing, Your Honour, from the Prosecution, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Nothing, Your Honour, and thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic, that concludes the proceedings for this morning. The court is now adjourned, and you will meantime remain in the custody of the Tribunal.
